title: Statistics: standardization, variation and probability bounds
mission: Curate atomic reusable algebraic statistics relationships: standardization, relative variation and distribution-free bounds, each with explicit population or sample scope. Descriptive and standardization arithmetic only; continue through successive batches with no inference chain required.
priorities: z-score standardization from value, mean and standard deviation
Coefficient of variation from standard deviation and mean
Chebyshev lower bound on within-k-sigma probability
Standardized mean difference from two group means and a supplied pooled spread
boundaries: Population vs sample meanings must be explicit in every record; means and spreads are supplied inputs, never computed from raw data here (no arrays).
Estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, ANOVA and likelihood methods are excluded.
Forms needing sqrt, exp or log (standard error, normal PDF/CDF, confidence intervals, pooled-spread computation) must be deferred with sources, never approximated.
Probability identities belong to the probability lane: reference them, do not duplicate them.
starter_sources: https://openstax.org -- navigate to an Introductory Statistics title and its chapters on descriptive statistics and discrete distributions; record exact book, edition and section, never cite the root as evidence
No further source URLs were preverified for this assignment; discovery snippets alone do not prove the equation
special_checks: Guard positive spread and nonzero mean where required; retain z-score signs, never absolutize silently
Chebyshev records must state the k>1 scope where the bound is nontrivial and test a boundary case
The pooled spread in the standardized-difference record is a supplied input with stated scope, not a computed estimate
Distinguish the algebraic bound from any distributional or empirical claim
integration_expectation: Dimensionless throughout; meanings (z_score, coefficient_of_variation, chebyshev_bound, standardized_difference and similar) are new and require extension. All seed forms are scalar and fit the engine once meanings exist.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
